<inputs>
Ask me for: the accent colour, a song (mp3), the words for the 3 text moments (search query, card title, toast). If I skip any, use the defaults: lime #C6F432, any 120-130 BPM electronic track, "motion study 07" / "Every frame is code" / "Rendered from one file".
</inputs>

<direction>
One black shape (#0e0e10) on a warm light stage (#f4f4f1 to #e1e1dc radial). It never cuts: every UI state is born out of the one before it. White text, Geist for UI, Geist Mono for numbers and labels. The accent appears only where something turns on.
A macOS cursor drives every change with real clicks and one real drag.
Every morph uses one curve: cubic-bezier(.45,0,.15,1). Pop-ins use a closed-form spring with a tiny overshoot. Text rises through a mask line, it never fades in.
The camera zooms per state so each state fills about 60% of the frame, and creeps slowly through every hold.
Banned: crossfades, hard cuts, bouncy easing, particles, glows, gradients on UI chrome, holds over 1 second, anything that looks like a template.
</direction>

<structure>
120 BPM grid, 24 beats, then the whole film is time-warped onto the real song's beat.
Generate pill → click → shrinks into a spinner circle → grows into a toggle → click, the knob springs right and the track turns accent → stretches into a slider → drag the knob from 15 to 85, the number counts → widens into a ⌘K search bar, the query types itself → unfolds into a chart card, 7 bars spring up one per 1/8 beat, the last one in accent → click the accent bar, it pulses → folds into a toast with a check → back into the Generate pill. Last frame = first frame, cursor included.
</structure>

<build>
1. One HTML file, square 1440x1440. Every style is computed from time inside seek(t): no CSS transitions, no timers, no state between frames.
2. The shape is one div. Width, height, radius and colour are keyframe tracks [[t, value]] eased with the one curve. Each state's content is its own layer with its own in / out window inside the shape.
3. Camera: one scale track around the centre, plus a 1.2% sine creep over the whole loop.
4. Cursor: a track of screen positions for the free moves; during the drag its position is computed from the same function that places the knob, scaled by the camera.
5. Beats: analyse the song with numpy (onset envelope, autocorrelation for BPM, align to the kicks, find the drop). Put the drop on the chart bars springing up.
6. Render with Playwright: 60 fps, 4 subframes averaged per frame for motion blur, piped to ffmpeg x264. Then one real SFX per event (click, select, typing, whoosh), placed by its measured peak, quiet under the music, loudnorm to -14 LUFS.
</build>

<inputs>
Ask me for: 8 to 12 UI states I want the shape to become (e.g. button, loader, player, slider, toggle, tabs, chart, command palette, toast), pure black and white or one accent color, and a royalty-free song around 120 BPM (e.g. Mixkit, free for commercial use).
</inputs>

<direction>
Dribbble-level UI motion. One shape, never cut: every state is the same element morphing its size, radius and color while its content swaps with a short blur. A cursor drives every change with real clicks and drags. Light warm-gray canvas, black and white components, one clean UI font (Geist). Springs everywhere, a tiny overshoot at most. The camera zooms so each state fills the frame. The last frame is the first frame, so it loops.
Banned: bouncy easing, particle bursts, glows, gradients on UI chrome, mismatched icon strokes, dead time, anything that looks like a template.
</direction>

<structure>
120 BPM, 7 bars, something happens on every beat.
Button → loader → check → dynamic island → music player with a play/pause morph → scrub the progress bar → it becomes a volume slider that stretches when dragged past max → a toggle flips on the beat → the knob becomes a liquid tab indicator → the tabs open into a chart that draws itself, with a tooltip on hover → it collapses into ⌘K → type to filter → enter → toast → back to the button.
</structure>

<build>
1. One HTML file, square 1440x1440. Every style is computed from time inside seek(t): no CSS transitions, no timers, no state carried between frames.
2. Springs are closed-form step responses. A value that changes target many times is the sum of one spring per change, so it stays a pure function of time.
3. The tab indicator's two edges ride different springs, so the leading edge stretches ahead of the trailing one. Same trick for the toggle knob.
4. Drags are direct manipulation: while the cursor is held, the value is computed from its position. On release it springs back from wherever it was.
5. Analyze the song with numpy for the beat grid and start on a downbeat. Place every UI sound by its measured peak.
6. Render with Playwright: 4 subframes per frame, blended with ffmpeg tmix for motion blur at 60fps.
7. Render one frame per beat before the full render. Fix anything off the grid, cramped or hard to read.
</build>

<gotchas>
Never put will-change on anything the camera scales or the text renders blurry. Text that swaps inside a morphing container needs its own enter and exit timing or it overlaps. Make the last frame identical to the first, cursor position and speed included, or the loop stutters.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me for the inputs, then show me the state list on the beat grid before you write any code.
</start>
